sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year, from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $332 billion in FY2026 [F221][F1][F10].
Operating income compounded faster at 20.5% [F223], lifting operating margin from 30.1% [F41] to 46.8% [F50].
The largest margin step came in FY2021, when operating margin rose 4.6pp to 41.6% [D220][F45].
The filings tie part of that year's gross margin gain to a change in the estimated useful lives of server and network equipment [P55][D219].
Intelligent Cloud contributed 11.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth [D917][D472], more than any other segment.
Productivity and Business Processes added 6.8pp [D892], while More Personal Computing subtracted 0.2pp [D942].
The filing credits Microsoft Cloud for the growth, which supplied 16.2pp of the 17.8% increase [P17][D568][D472].
Microsoft Cloud now makes up 64.6% of revenue [D566], so growth depends heavily on one category.
Operating income grew 20.8% [D473] on a 53.3% incremental margin [D498], so profit outran revenue growth of 17.8% [D472].
Operating margin of 46.8% [F50] equals the window high [D974] and sits well above the 41.7% median [D975].
In FY2026 cost of revenue took 0.9pp off operating margin [D500], offset by R&D at +0.8pp [D501] and other lines at +1.2pp [D502].
Company gross margin fell 0.9pp to 67.9% [D486][F30], and the MD&A ties the Intelligent Cloud dip to AI infrastructure investment [P11].
Operating expenses grew 7.4% [D491], which the MD&A ties to R&D compute capacity, AI talent and XBOX impairment charges [P16].
Net margin rose 4.2pp [D488], well above operating margin's 1.2pp [D487], because other income turned positive [X124][P7].
Operating cash flow was 1.37x net income [D459], but free cash flow was only 0.50x [D460], the window low [D988].
Capex rose 79.6% to $116 billion [D479][F110], and the filing cites a $51.4 billion rise in property and equipment additions [P1].
Operating cash flow grew 34.4% [D477] against capex growth of 79.6% [D479], so free cash flow fell 6.5% [D478].
The squeeze reflects spending rather than weaker operations, but the cited filings do not say when capex will slow [D477].
Net cash was $72.9 billion [D465], 22.0% of revenue [D466], at the 83rd percentile of six software peers, against a median of -7.2% [D1006][D1007].
Net cash rose from $66.8 billion in FY2025 [D411] as debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion [D495][D464].
Buybacks and dividends totalled $48.7 billion [D467], 72.7% of free cash flow [D468], and the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D493].
Liquidity is thinner: the current ratio of 1.23x [F200] is its window low [D991], against a 1.93x median [D993].
Medium severity, persisting two years: free cash flow was 0.70x and 0.50x net income in FY2025 and FY2026 [D406][D460].
Capex rose 79.6% [D479] while operating cash flow grew 34.4% [D477], and the filing cites higher property and equipment additions [P1].
It matters because shareholder payouts equal 72.7% of free cash flow [D468], so they now rest on a thinner cash base.
Medium severity, one year: net income grew 31.3% [D474], ahead of operating income's 20.8% [D473], on other income of $10.7 billion [X124].
The filing attributes the swing mainly to $6.5 billion of net OpenAI gains, chiefly a dilution gain [P7].
In the FY2027 10-K, a free cash flow margin below 20.2% [D982] confirms the squeeze, and a recovery toward 30.3% [D984] reverses it.
In the FY2027 10-K, a gross margin below 67.9% [F30] confirms the cost pressure, and a return above the 68.2% median [D981] reverses it.
In the FY2027 10-K, other income falling from its FY2026 level of $10.7 billion [X124] toward the FY2025 loss of $4.9 billion [X123] would show net income leaning on the operating trend.
